page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by the AWS Nitro System and an Intel Xeon 8175M processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware configuration adheres to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no integrated local storage and features no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage over its 20 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark data reveals a marked contrast between single-core and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core evaluations place the instance in the bottom 25%, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1286.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1039.0. Conversely, parallel execution scales effectively across the 64 virtual cores, yielding average tier results such as 54159.82 in stress-ng multi-core and 43191.13 in PassMark CPU tests. A notable strength is its uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 192.72 GB/sec for large-block reads and 90.92 GB/sec for large-block writes, both performing within the top 25%.

Application tests reflect moderate performance across standard service profiles, delivering 50.81 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 36.27 GB/sec in static web serving. Text generation during large language model inference is constrained by single-thread capability, but the instance provides ample resource density for enterprise software builds, multi-threaded data transformations, backend web clusters, and memory-resident caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based cloud instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Built on an Intel Xeon 8175M processor operating at 3.1 GHz across 32 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 20 Gbps of baseline networking capacity, contains zero local storage, and does not bundle GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, the m5.16xlarge shows weak single-core execution speed alongside dependable middle-tier multi-threaded performance, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 43191.13. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth ranks in the top quartile, sustaining 192.72 GB/sec read throughput. Although single-threaded tasks and generative language model inference operate slowly, its high core count and stable multi-core throughput make it appropriate for parallelized enterprise workloads, multi-threaded compilation, backend web application pools, and mid-tier distributed caching architectures using network-attached volumes.
